name: Does sub-trade coordination for electrical cost extra, or does it save money?

mainEntity.name: Does sub-trade coordination for electrical cost extra, or does it save money?

acceptedAnswer.text: Coordination itself is usually part of the project management or general contracting scope, but extra cost can come from redesign, missed handoffs, emergency return visits, or change orders. If the electrical scope is unclear, the price can rise because the electrician has to revisit the site or adjust work after other trades have already moved on. Clear plans up front are the most cost-effective way to control the electrical budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: It usually saves money overall by preventing rework, missed handoffs, and costly change orders.
